shot.vai: nhận ra nơi chốn: ngày → đêm từ giây 0 (TL-5, §14.7)
cau: This is the City of London, seen from Bankside, across the Thames.
Among the towers stands one dome — and much of this skyline is shaped to keep it in view.
We are standing near where Samuel Pepys stood on the second night of the Great Fire.

shot.vai: luận đề: toà cao lún xuống, mái vòm tan, Old St Paul's hiện lại
cau: London has burned to the ground twice.
Twice, it got the chance to start over.
And twice, it rebuilt itself on its old, crooked streets.

shot.vai: KHOẢNH KHẮC GIÁ TRỊ NHẤT ≤ 30 s: "one entire arch of fire" nhìn từ chỗ Pepys đứng
cau: Look closely, and the old street pattern is still there, threading between the towers.

shot.vai: cú lặn từ cao xuống Pudding Lane — "a bakery about a kilometre from here"
cau: To see why, we go back to a Sunday night in September 1666 — to a bakery about a kilometre from here.

shot.vai: M-d (1) Pudding Lane 01:00 — đốm lửa trong lò bánh
cau: Sunday, the second of September 1666.
At about one in the morning, fire breaks out in Pudding Lane, in the house of Thomas Farriner, baker to the King.

shot.vai: lửa lớn dần ở chân cầu; nhà gỗ sát nhau; gió đông (khói sang tây)
cau: London is a city of timber.
Its houses are packed so tight that their upper storeys almost touch across the lanes.

shot.vai: Hollar vẽ từ St Saviour's: tranh khắc hoà vào 3D cùng góc (chú thích ≤ 6 từ thay thẻ)
cau: Nineteen years earlier, the engraver Wenceslaus Hollar had published a long view of this skyline, drawn from St Saviour's church, just along the bank: a forest of church towers, and above them all, the long roof of Old St Paul's.

shot.vai: St Magnus + Fish Street cháy; tới Steelyard trưa
cau: The summer has been dry, and a fierce east wind is blowing.
By morning, the fire has taken the church of St Magnus and most of Fish Street, at the foot of London Bridge.

shot.vai: M-d (2) bờ sông gần cầu: ném đồ xuống sà lan
cau: Samuel Pepys hurries to Whitehall and tells the King that unless houses are pulled down, nothing can stop the fire.
The King sends him to the Lord Mayor with that order.

shot.vai: Pepys gặp Thị trưởng ở Cannon Street; lửa vượt sức phá nhà
cau: The Lord Mayor, Sir Thomas Bludworth, is overwhelmed.
Pepys finds him in Cannon Street, a handkerchief round his neck: "Lord, what can I do?
I am spent.
People will not obey me."
"I have been pulling down houses, but the fire overtakes us faster than we can do it."

shot.vai: khoảng trống 1633 trên cầu chặn lửa sang Southwark; gió đẩy lửa sang tây
cau: London Bridge survives.
A gap left by an earlier fire, in 1633, stops the flames from crossing to Southwark.
Instead, the wind drives the fire west, along the waterfront, and up the hill.

shot.vai: Pepys ở quán bia Bankside: chạng vạng → vòng cung lửa
cau: That evening, Pepys takes shelter in "a little ale-house on the Bankside" — about where we are standing.
As it grows dark, he sees "one entire arch of fire" — more than a mile long.
"It made me weep to see it."

shot.vai: BẢN ĐỒ CỔ HOẠT HOÁ: Doornick 1666, lửa lan theo ngày, chuyển 3D cùng toạ độ
cau: Monday.
The fire spreads up Gracechurch Street to Lombard Street, and west to Cannon Street.
At two in the afternoon, it takes the Royal Exchange — the City's trading floor.

shot.vai: M-d (4) Watling Street: xe, người khiêng, người bệnh
cau: The roads are jammed with carts.

shot.vai: Royal Exchange cháy; trời "như miệng lò"
cau: John Evelyn walks the burning streets that night.
The sky, he writes, is "like the top of a burning oven"; the noise is "like a hideous storm" — the cracking of the flames, the fall of towers, houses and churches.

shot.vai: M-d (3) Thames: sà lan, đồ trôi, bờ bắc rực lửa
cau: The river fills with boats — and with goods floating on the water.

shot.vai: lửa leo đồi Ludgate tới Old St Paul's có giàn giáo; nhà thờ bốc cháy
cau: Tuesday, the fourth.
The fire climbs Ludgate Hill to St Paul's Cathedral, wrapped in wooden scaffolding for repairs.
By evening, the great church is ablaze.

shot.vai: M-d (5) chì chảy quanh St Paul's
cau: John Evelyn watches its lead run down the streets "in a stream".

shot.vai: nổ nhà bằng thuốc súng ở Tower Street (lớp a, render); Pepys chôn rượu + phô mai
cau: In the west, the fire crosses the Fleet and runs down Fleet Street, as far as the Temple.
Only now are houses blown up with gunpowder to open firebreaks — first in Tower Street, near the Tower.
At the Navy Office, Pepys and a colleague dig a pit in the garden for their wine — and Pepys buries his Parmesan cheese.

shot.vai: gió dịu; lửa tàn; bình minh 5/9
cau: That night, the wind finally drops.
By Thursday, the fire is out.

shot.vai: M-d (7) Moorfields: lều, chòi, đống đồ
cau: Homeless Londoners camp in the fields outside the walls — Moorfields, St George's Fields, as far as Highgate — "some under tents, some under miserable huts and hovels."

shot.vai: phế tích bốc khói: ranh vùng cháy + bộ đếm 13 200 nhà / 87 nhà thờ
cau: About thirteen thousand two hundred houses.
Eighty-seven parish churches.
St Paul's.
Roughly four-fifths of the City — over four hundred acres.
Fewer than ten deaths were recorded.
The real toll is unknown.

shot.vai: M-d (8) phế tích bốc khói
Evelyn đi trên phế tích: chỉ nhận ra nơi nhờ tháp còn đứng
cau: The ashes are still warm when the plans arrive.
When Evelyn walks through the ruins, he cannot tell where he is — except by the shell of some church or hall, with a tower still standing.

shot.vai: phương án Wren (bản in LoC 1767) đặt khớp lên City cháy — không được dựng
cau: Within days, Christopher Wren hands the King a new City on paper — straight avenues, open squares, a grid.
John Evelyn draws another.
Robert Hooke, a third.
None of them is built.
Wren's plan survives only on paper — engraved and sold a century later as the London that might have been.

shot.vai: lô đất rối; Toà Cháy ở Clifford's Inn (vùng không cháy)
cau: Every plot in the burnt City has its owners — and the people who have lost their homes cannot afford to wait years for it all to be redrawn.
So Parliament moves faster.
From late February 1667, a special Fire Court sits at Clifford's Inn, settling disputes between landlords and tenants.
In its first year, it decides three hundred and seventy-four cases.

shot.vai: Rebuilding Act: tường gạch, 4 hạng nhà theo hạng phố
cau: A Rebuilding Act sets the rules: outside walls of brick or stone, not timber.
Four classes of house — two storeys on the by-lanes, three on streets of note, four on the high streets, and four for mansions of the greatest size.
And a new duty on coal pays for the City's public buildings.

shot.vai: timelapse xây lại bằng gạch trên đúng lô cũ (≈ 6 000 nhà cuối 1670)
cau: The old street plan stays.
Two new streets — King Street and Queen Street — are cut down from the Guildhall toward the river.
Rebuilding gets going in 1668.
By the end of 1670, about six thousand new houses are up — on the same lanes, in brick.
City surveyors — Hooke among them — stake out the widened streets, then the old foundations, plot by plot.

shot.vai: Monument mọc; vạch 202 ft nối tới lò bánh Pudding Lane
cau: Near the bakery, Wren and Hooke raise a column: the Monument.
Two hundred and two feet high — exactly the distance to the spot in Pudding Lane where the fire began.

shot.vai: Barbon lập Fire Office — dấu bảo hiểm trên mặt nhà [vật minh hoạ: cần kiểm]
cau: Fire insurance begins here too.
In 1680, Nicholas Barbon opens the Fire Office.

shot.vai: chóp nhà thờ Wren trắng mọc quanh City
cau: Wren's office rebuilds fifty-one of the City's churches.

shot.vai: St Paul's mới mọc từ nền Old St Paul's
cau: And on Ludgate Hill, where Old St Paul's stood, work starts in 1675 on a new cathedral.

shot.vai: đèn lồng hoàn tất; 365 ft — mái vòm anh hùng giờ vàng
cau: The last stone of the lantern is set in 1708.
In 1711, Parliament declares St Paul's complete — three hundred and sixty-five feet, to the top of the cross.

shot.vai: Ogilby & Morgan 1676 đặt trùng lưới phố 1666: cùng tuyến phố
then–now: khung Hollar ↔ cùng khung 1711
từ phía đông: City gạch + mái vòm, sông có thuyền tiền cảnh
cần cẩu hạ: City gạch đã kín lô, mái vòm hoàn tất
mái vòm cao nhất > 250 năm; chóp Wren
cau: For more than two and a half centuries, nothing in London stands taller than the dome.

shot.vai: nhà trên cầu dỡ (1761); cầu mới 1831
cau: On London Bridge, the houses and shops are pulled down in 1758.
By 1831, a new bridge has replaced the medieval one.

shot.vai: Victoria Embankment đẩy bờ bắc ra sông (bờ 1666 ↔ 2026)
cau: Wren's steeples ring the dome.
Around it, the City keeps changing, building by building.
Even the river moves.
Between 1864 and 1870, the Victoria Embankment pushes the north bank out into the Thames.

shot.vai: toà văn phòng chen quanh nhà thờ; phố bên dưới không đổi
cau: In the 1930s, taller office blocks begin to rise near the cathedral, blocking some of its best-known views.
But the lanes underneath hardly shift.

shot.vai: St Paul's Heights: mặt phẳng trần cao độ hiện mờ quanh mái vòm
cau: In 1937, the cathedral's surveyor, Godfrey Allen, proposes a rule: new buildings must stay low enough to keep the dome in sight from the Thames bridges and the south bank.
From 1938, the City applies it.
It is called the St Paul's Heights.

shot.vai: cùng khung Bankside: 1938 ↔ 1666
chạng vạng mùa đông; Chủ nhật
cau: Sunday, the twenty-ninth of December, 1940.
In 1666, the fire took four days.
This time, the worst of it comes in a single night.

shot.vai: bom cháy rơi thành tia; ≈ 1 500 đám cháy; bộ đếm 100 000
cau: As dusk falls, German bombers begin dropping incendiaries on the City — at least a hundred thousand of them.
Around fifteen hundred fires.

shot.vai: triều thấp: bãi bùn, vòi rồng không tới nước [cần kiểm]
cau: It is a Sunday.
Many offices are locked and unattended.
The water mains are broken, and the Thames is at low tide.

shot.vai: KHOẢNH KHẮC MÁI VÒM giữa khói lửa (dựng 3D thay ảnh Mason — T4-G1); Paternoster Row cháy
cau: Next to St Paul's, the booksellers' street, Paternoster Row, burns — and with it as many as five million books.
Fire crews and volunteers of the St Paul's Watch fight the bombs that land on the cathedral itself.
Across the City, the Guildhall's roof burns, and nineteen churches are destroyed.
Winston Churchill reportedly sends word that St Paul's must be saved at all costs.

shot.vai: sáng ra: mái vòm còn đứng; 1 ảnh MOI 1940 (Crown PD) góc khung
cau: By morning, the dome is still standing, in a ring of ruins.

shot.vai: vòng phế tích quanh mái vòm; bộ đếm 160
cau: About a hundred and sixty people are killed that night — at least twelve of them firefighters.

shot.vai: vùng bom nặng Cripplegate / Paternoster (ước lượng — KHÔNG dùng LCC Bomb Damage Maps)
cau: For the second time in three centuries, a great stretch of the City lies in ruins.

shot.vai: hai khoảng trống cùng một khung
Holden–Holford: quy hoạch lại vùng bom
cau: And for the second time, the planners arrive with a clean sheet.
In 1946 and 1947, Charles Holden and William Holford draw up a new plan for the City.

shot.vai: London Wall (Route 11) + Barbican mọc trên Cripplegate
cau: Where the bombs hit hardest, it is bold: a new road, London Wall, built in the 1950s; and on the ruins of Cripplegate, from the mid-1960s, the towers of the Barbican.

shot.vai: lưới phố Doornick 1666 chồng lên 3D 2026: cùng tuyến
cau: Everywhere else, it keeps most of the old street lines.
The lanes come back.

shot.vai: cụm toà cao phía đông mọc lên
cau: Slowly, the gaps fill again.
Today, more than six hundred thousand people work in the City — the Square Mile.
And in this century, a cluster of towers climbs to the east, around Bishopsgate and Leadenhall Street.

shot.vai: từ Fleet Street: Leadenhall vát — mái vòm còn nền trời
cau: So when the towers arrive, they rise on the old street pattern — and under the dome's rules.
The St Paul's Heights still apply, alongside a set of protected views across London — the farthest from a hill in Richmond Park, ten miles away.
New towers must also respect protected views of the dome from Parliament Hill, Primrose Hill and Greenwich Park — and from King Henry's Mound in Richmond Park.
The Leadenhall Building tapers as it rises, so that from Fleet Street, the dome still has open sky behind it.

shot.vai: vòng 30° quanh mái vòm từ phía đông
KHÉP VÒNG: cùng khung Bankside — vòng cung lửa ↔ đèn City
cau: From Bankside tonight, you can stand roughly where Pepys stood, and look across at the same streets.
London burned twice.
Twice, it could have started over.
Twice, it kept its old streets.
And the skyline it built still bends around the one building it chose, again and again, to keep in view.

shot.vai: kéo lùi cuối: mái vòm giữa toà cao
hai thẻ "How this film was made" × 8 s (§12.1 b)
